results.name: single_example_magnitude_gradient
results.description: For single-example sets, yes rate for targets within 10 of the example minus yes rate for targets more than 30 away (excluding same-final-digit targets); observed above null means people generalise by magnitude similarity more steeply than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: single_example_magnitude_gradient
# description: For single-example sets, yes rate for targets within 10 of the example minus yes rate for targets more than 30 away (excluding same-final-digit targets); observed above null means people generalise by magnitude similarity more steeply than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    u = pd.unique(s)
    codes = pd.Categorical(s, categories=u).codes
    U = np.full((len(u), 4), np.nan)
    for i, x in enumerate(u):
        v = [int(float(z)) for z in x.split(",") if z.strip() != ""][:4]
        U[i, :len(v)] = v
    E = U[codes]
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1)
    hi = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    Ed = np.mod(E, 10)
    td = np.mod(t, 10)
    shares_last = np.any(Ed == td[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    in_set = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    first = Ed[:, 0]
    all_same_last = np.all((Ed == first[:, None]) | np.isnan(Ed), axis=1)
    base = (n == 1) & ~in_set & ~shares_last
    a = base & (dist <= 10)
    b = base & (dist > 30)
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: decade_match_outside_range_contrast
results.description: Among targets >5 outside the set range that share no final digit with any example, yes rate for targets sharing a tens digit with some example minus yes rate for those that do not; observed above null means people use decade similarity the model lacks.

# description: Among targets >5 outside the set range that share no final digit with any example, yes rate for targets sharing a tens digit with some example minus yes rate for those that do not; observed above null means people use decade similarity the model lacks.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    u = pd.unique(s)
    codes = pd.Categorical(s, categories=u).codes
    U = np.full((len(u), 4), np.nan)
    for i, x in enumerate(u):
        v = [int(float(z)) for z in x.split(",") if z.strip() != ""][:4]
        U[i, :len(v)] = v
    E = U[codes]
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1)
    hi = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    Ed = np.mod(E, 10)
    td = np.mod(t, 10)
    shares_last = np.any(Ed == td[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    in_set = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    first = Ed[:, 0]
    all_same_last = np.all((Ed == first[:, None]) | np.isnan(Ed), axis=1)
    def tens(a):
        return np.where(a >= 100, 10, np.floor(a / 10))

    a = base & sd
    b = base & ~sd
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: shared_contained_digit_nonfinal_yes
results.description: Yes rate for targets containing (in any position) a digit present in every example of a >=2-example set, but sharing no final digit with any example and >5 from every example; observed above null means people generalise contained-digit rules more than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: shared_contained_digit_nonfinal_yes
# description: Yes rate for targets containing (in any position) a digit present in every example of a >=2-example set, but sharing no final digit with any example and >5 from every example; observed above null means people generalise contained-digit rules more than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    u = pd.unique(s)
    codes = pd.Categorical(s, categories=u).codes
    U = np.full((len(u), 4), np.nan)
    for i, x in enumerate(u):
        v = [int(float(z)) for z in x.split(",") if z.strip() != ""][:4]
        U[i, :len(v)] = v
    E = U[codes]
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1)
    hi = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    Ed = np.mod(E, 10)
    td = np.mod(t, 10)
    shares_last = np.any(Ed == td[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    in_set = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    first = Ed[:, 0]
    all_same_last = np.all((Ed == first[:, None]) | np.isnan(Ed), axis=1)
    def digs(a):
        a = np.nan_to_num(a, nan=-1).astype(int)
        out = np.zeros(a.shape + (10,), bool)
        for d in range(10):
            out[..., d] = (a >= 0) & ((a % 10 == d) | ((a >= 10) & ((a // 10) % 10 == d)) | ((a >= 100) & (a // 100 == d)))
        return out
    valid = ~np.isnan(E)
    common = np.all(digs(E) | ~valid[..., None], axis=1)
    has = np.any(common & digs(t), axis=1)
    m = (n >= 2) & has & ~shares_last & (dist > 5) & ~in_set
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: arithmetic_relation_target_excess_v2
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets equal to a sum, absolute difference, double or half of examples minus yes rate of other targets (all restricted to no shared final digit and >3 from every example); observed above null means people use arithmetic relations between examples that the model lacks.
results.code:
# name: arithmetic_relation_target_excess_v2
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets equal to a sum, absolute difference, double or half of examples minus yes rate of other targets (all restricted to no shared final digit and >3 from every example); observed above null means people use arithmetic relations between examples that the model lacks.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    u = pd.unique(s)
    codes = pd.Categorical(s, categories=u).codes
    U = np.full((len(u), 4), np.nan)
    for i, x in enumerate(u):
        v = [int(float(z)) for z in x.split(",") if z.strip() != ""][:4]
        U[i, :len(v)] = v
    E = U[codes]
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1)
    hi = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    Ed = np.mod(E, 10)
    td = np.mod(t, 10)
    shares_last = np.any(Ed == td[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    in_set = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    first = Ed[:, 0]
    all_same_last = np.all((Ed == first[:, None]) | np.isnan(Ed), axis=1)
    rel = np.zeros(len(t), bool)
    for i in range(4):
        rel |= (E[:, i] * 2 == t) | (E[:, i] / 2 == t)
        for j in range(i + 1, 4):
            rel |= (E[:, i] + E[:, j] == t) | (np.abs(E[:, i] - E[:, j]) == t)
    base = ~in_set & ~shares_last & (dist > 3)
    a = base & rel
    b = base & ~rel
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())
